faqs.q: How do I use the IT salary guide Melbourne calculator?
faqs.a: Enter your base hourly rate (before casual loading) into the timesheet on the home page. If you work casual hours, check the 'casual loading' box to add 25% on top. The calculator then shows your gross annual pay (hourly × hours per week × 52), fortnightly pay (weekly × 2), estimated tax using the 2026–27 resident rates plus Medicare levy, and superannuation at 12% of ordinary earnings. All figures assume a 38-hour week unless you adjust the hours.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave entitlements. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading. This loading is applied before calculating super and tax. The calculator adds it automatically when you select the casual loading checkbox – never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at the 12% guarantee rate (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your hourly rate or salary. For example, if your gross annual pay is $52,000, your employer must contribute an additional $6,240 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The calculator shows this estimated super amount separately.

bodyMarkdown:
## IT Salary Guide Melbourne: Understanding Your Pay

Whether you're an IT contractor, a casual developer, or a permanent employee negotiating a salary in Melbourne, converting your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and monthly figures helps you compare offers. Our IT salary guide Melbourne tool uses the latest Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission rates, including the 25% casual loading and the 12% super guarantee paid on top.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a 38-hour week, which is the ordinary full-time hours under most awards and the National Minimum Wage. If you work different hours, you can adjust the weekly hours in the calculator. For example, a $50 per hour IT contractor working 38 hours a week earns:

$50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800 per year (before tax and super).

Fortnightly pay is simply weekly pay × 2. So $50 × 38 = $1,900 per week, or $3,800 per fortnight.

### Casual Loading: Adding 25% on Top

Many IT roles are casual or contract, attracting a 25% casual loading. This is an extra payment on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual, sick, personal). The calculator has a checkbox to add this loading automatically. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading – the calculator applies it correctly.

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour. With casual loading, that becomes $33.05 per hour. Most IT awards have higher minimum rates, but the loading principle is the same. Check your specific award using the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top, Not Deducted

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026) and is paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It does not reduce your take-home pay. For example, on a $98,800 annual salary, your employer contributes an additional $11,856 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

The calculator shows estimated super separately. Remember, super is not included in the annual gross figure – it's an extra benefit.

### Minimum Award Wages and the National Minimum Wage

Most employees are covered by a modern award. From 1 July 2026, minimum award wages increased by 4.75%, with the lowest rate in any award at least $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week. The Fair Work Commission sets these rates. If you are award-free, the National Minimum Wage applies. Casual employees get the 25% loading on top.

For IT professionals, common awards include the Professional Employees Award and the Clerks Award. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool to find your exact rate.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Our calculator uses the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Plus Medicare levy at 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 were not confirmed). The tax estimate is for a single resident claiming the full tax-free threshold. It does not include HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Example: IT Contractor in Melbourne

Consider a casual IT contractor in Melbourne earning $60 per hour (base rate). With casual loading, the effective rate becomes $75 per hour. For a 38-hour week:

- Weekly: $75 × 38 = $2,850
- Fortnightly: $5,700
- Annual gross: $148,200
- Estimated tax (including Medicare): ~$37,000
- Estimated super (12%): $17,784

This gives a clear picture of total remuneration. Compare this with a permanent salary offer of, say, $130,000 plus super – the contractor may come out ahead when factoring in flexibility and higher hourly rates.

### Using the Calculator

Start at [the timesheet](/), enter your base hourly rate, and select casual loading if applicable. The results show annual, fortnightly, and monthly figures, plus estimated tax and super. You can also explore [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for more details.

### Important Notes

This calculator provides estimates only. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For precise pay rates, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) and the Fair Work Commission's National Minimum Wage Order. For tax, consult the Australian Taxation Office.
